extracted.intended_audience: readers researching the Bourbaki Éléments de mathématique and designers/authors of rigorous mathematics texts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and descriptive standards for producing a large-scale, rigorous mathematical textbook/treatise in the style of Bourbaki (organization, content types, logical dependencies, publication practices). Useful for authors or editors planning a formal mathematics series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained formal treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The series is noted as a large-scale, self-contained, formal treatment of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should aim to be self-contained and formal: present material so a reader can follow without requiring external sources for prerequisite definitions and fundamental results. Emphasizes formal rigor and comprehensive internal development of topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter composition: definitions, notation, proofs, exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapters present definitions, mathematical notation, proofs of theorems and exercises, forming the core mathematical content of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each chapter should include clear definitions and notation, rigorous proofs for stated theorems, and exercises for practice. This is the expected canonical structure for chapters in a Bourbaki-style treatise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary historical notes and summaries of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapters are supplemented by historical notes and summaries of results. The former usually appear after a chapter to contextualize topics; the latter collect a book's major results and may state them without proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include historical context to situate developments and optional concise 'Summary of Results' sections that list main theorems (possibly without proofs) for reference and orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract Packet / foundational prerequisites included from scratch
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders conceived an introductory and foundational section (the 'Abstract Packet') to describe all prerequisite concepts from scratch; this portion was realized as the first three books (set theory, abstract algebra, general topology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an explicit foundational section covering prerequisites so later chapters can assume those foundations. This supports the self-contained nature of the work and clarifies what is assumed versus developed in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical ordering and dependency of chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the Fundamental Structures of Analysis, any statements or proofs presented within a given chapter assume as given the results established in previous chapters; the first six books are 'logically ordered' so each section takes as given all preceding material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize material so logical dependencies are explicit and later material builds only on earlier established results. When publishing out of logical order, ensure later-published material is grounded by later publication of logically earlier chapters or make dependencies explicit in front matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unanimous group approval before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The group's working style is slow and rigorous, and a final product is not deemed acceptable unless it is unanimously approved by the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt rigorous internal review and require broad (in Bourbaki's case unanimous) approval before finalizing and publishing a volume. Expect slow, careful consensus-driven editorial processes as a quality-control mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Results as a distinct device
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Summary of Results' was a section that collected the Theory of Sets' main results, stating them without proof; although it was the first item published, it does not count toward the chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Summary of Results' sections when appropriate to give readers a compact statement of principal outcomes, but be explicit whether such summaries are considered formal chapters or auxiliary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication format: fascicules then collected volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Volumes were originally published as small installments (fascicules) and later collected and reprinted in larger volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider publishing incremental installments for parts of a large work and later compiling them into complete volumes; maintain bibliographical clarity about fascicule/volume numbering and the relationship between installments and collected editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and edition fidelity / completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The large majority of the Éléments has been translated into English, although the translation is incomplete; some English editions are not based on the latest revised French editions and may miss material added there (example: General Topology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing translations or new editions, ensure translations reflect the latest revised source editions and note differences or omissions; maintain versioning and editorial notes so readers know which edition underlies a translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive scope across core mathematical branches
rubrics_metrics.description: The series expanded from analysis to cover several branches: set theory, abstract algebra, topology, analysis, Lie groups and Lie algebras, spectral theory, differential and analytic manifolds, algebraic topology, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for broad, coherent scope across foundational and advanced branches when designing a comprehensive treatise; plan the arc of the work so interdependencies between areas are recognized and addressed in the ordering or foundational material.
